prompt: Open two AuditSinks in one try-with-resources and report the failure that escaped plus every exception it suppressed, in the order getSuppressed() returns them.
explanation: When the body of a try-with-resources throws and a close() throws as well, Java keeps the body's exception as the one that propagates and attaches the close failure to it via addSuppressed, so no information is lost. getSuppressed() returns those extra exceptions as an array in the order they were attached, which is the reverse order the resources were declared in. If the body succeeds there is no primary exception to attach to, so the first failing close() becomes the exception that escapes and later ones are suppressed onto it.
hints: Declare both resources in one statement: try (AuditSink a = first; AuditSink b = second) { ... }. Do not write two nested try blocks.
Catch Throwable, not just IllegalStateException -- then read primary.getMessage() and loop over primary.getSuppressed().
Return "ok" only after the try statement finishes without an exception; the catch block returns the report string.
